root_cause: Three issues prevent correct keyboard and pointer behavior: (1) The datepicker passes `inputMode: !this._isInline` to Vanilla Calendar Pro, enabling input mode for non-inline calendars which traps the Tab key inside the calendar widget. (2) The data-api click handler explicitly skips input elements, relying solely on focusin to show the calendar, but focusin may not fire in all test environments. (3) The `_onOutside` dismiss handler treats the trigger element as "outside" because `element.contains(element)` returns false, causing the calendar to hide immediately when the input receives focusin from a click. Additionally, the click handler's `event.preventDefault()` for inputs may interfere with focusin firing in some test environments.
repair_strategy: Make three minimal changes to js/src/datepicker.ts: (1) Set `inputMode: false` in `_buildCalendarOptions` so Tab can escape the calendar. (2) Update the data-api click handler to call `instance.show()` for input elements (without `event.preventDefault()`) instead of skipping them, ensuring the calendar appears on click in all environments while preserving toggle behavior for non-input elements. (3) Fix `_onOutside` in `_setupDismiss` to exclude the trigger element (`target !== this._element`) from the outside check so focusin on the trigger doesn't close the calendar.
expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab when the datepicker calendar is open moves focus to the next focusable element (passengers field) instead of being trapped. Clicking the departure date input reliably shows the calendar. Focusin on the input also shows the calendar. Non-input toggle elements still toggle the calendar.
functional_risks: Other keyboard navigation within the calendar (arrow keys, Enter, Escape) could be altered if they depended on inputMode being true
Inline calendars retain inputMode: false (unchanged behavior)

The outside-click dismiss logic now treats the trigger element as inside, which is correct for focusin but could theoretically affect pointerdown on the trigger; however pointerdown on the trigger is already handled by VCP internally
Removing preventDefault on input click may allow default browser behavior (e.g., text selection) but should not affect calendar functionality
verification_requirements: Verify Tab moves focus from departure date to passengers field when calendar is open
Verify arrow keys, Enter, and Escape still function correctly in the calendar
Verify clicking the departure date input shows the calendar
Verify focusin on the departure date input still shows the calendar
Verify non-input toggle elements still toggle the calendar
Verify clicking outside the calendar hides it
Verify pressing Escape closes the calendar
